sources.quote: ニンテンドー ゲームキューブ用８cmディスク

sources.method: 8 cm × 10 = 80 mm, from Nintendo Japan's Wii console page 'ニンテンドー ゲームキューブ用８cmディスク' (https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/console/index.html).

sources.quote: 3 inch Nintendo GameCube Disc based on Matsushita's Optical Disc Technology, approx 1.5GB Capacity

sources.method: 3 in × 25.4 = 76.2 mm, from Nintendo of Europe's '3 inch Nintendo GameCube Disc' (https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Hardware/Nintendo-History/Nintendo-GameCube/Technical-Details/Technical-Details-627134.html); a nominal size class, computed only to record the conflict.

conflicts.reason: Both are Nintendo's nominal size classes, not measurements: Nintendo Japan says 8 cm, Nintendo of Europe '3 inch'. 8 cm is the metric class the disc is made to (the 80 mm mini-disc size); '3 inch' is the customary imperial name for it. Chosen: 80. Measure a specimen to settle the real outer diameter.

notes: Nintendo of Europe: '3 inch Nintendo GameCube Disc based on Matsushita's Optical Disc Technology, approx 1.5GB Capacity'. Nintendo Japan (Wii page, backward-compatibility list): 'ゲームキューブ用８cmディスク'. Thickness and centre hole are not published by Nintendo, and no public standard covers this proprietary disc: null. shell null (Nintendo says nothing either way).
